title: System Requirements (March 2026)
content: This document describes the specifications and precautions that your computer must meet to install, launch, and operate Marvelous Designer software. # **Windows** Category | **Minimum** | **Recommended** ---|---|--- OS | Windows 11 64-bit (24H2) 1) | Windows 11 64-bit (25H2) Processor | AMD® Ryzen™ 3000 series Intel® 8th-Gen series | AMD® Ryzen™ 9000 series or higher Intel® i9 14th-Gen or higher Memory | 16GB | 64GB 2) Graphics card | AMD, Intel, Nvidia GPUs supporting OpenGL 1.6 or higher | NVIDIA® GeForce RTX 4000 series or NVIDIA® RTX A, RTX Ada, RTX Pro Blackwell series 3) 4) 5) Storage | SSD 10GB or more | SSD 20GB or more Screen | 1920x1080(FHD) | 2560x1440(QHD), 3840x2160(UHD, 4K) Input device | 3-button mouse | 3-button mouse Network | Internet connection required | Internet connection required 1) [Windows 10 support has ended on October 14, 2025](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/windows-10-support-has-ended-on-october-14-2025-2ca8b313-1946-43d3-b55c-2b95b107f281). Strongly recommend using Windows 11. 2) To use the basic functions of Marvelous Designer, 16GB of memory is required; for smoother operation, 32GB of memory is needed; and for very heavy and complex clothing and animations, 64GB or more of memory is required. 3) Marvelous Designer utilizes [Nvidia CUDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA) acceleration technology for Marvelous Designer GPU-Simulation and Rendering. So computers with only Intel Graphics or AMD graphics card do not benefit from GPU acceleration that speeds up Marvelous Designer simulation. If you want faster GPU-simulation in Marvelous Designer software, look for a computer with a recent Nvidia graphics card. 4) For graphics card related issues, please see the following guide. In particular, please update your graphics card driver to the latest. [Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358166752793) 5) A GPU that supports OpenGL Compatibility Profile 1.3 or higher is required to run Marvelous Designer software. Some mobile GPU processors from AMD and Intel may not fully support [OpenGL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenGL), which is essential for running Marvelous Designer software, and may not run Marvelous Designer software. If you are using a laptop or graphics card with a built-in CPU, check with the hardware manufacturer for the GPU model and whether it supports OpenGL. * * * # **Mac** Category | **Minimum** | **Recommended** ---|---|--- Mac models | Apple Silicon Mac: M11) | Apple Silicon Macs: M1, M2, M3, M4 macOS | Sonoma 14 *For macOS dependencies, check out the notes below 2) | Sequoia 15, Tahoe 26 Processor | Apple Silicon Chip | Apple Silicon Chip Memory | 16GB | 64GB 3) Storage | SSD 10GB or more | SSD 20GB or more Screen | 1920x1080 (FHD) | Retina 4K, Retina 5K supported Input devices | 3-button mouse | 3-button mouse Network | Internet connection required | Internet connection required 1) [Apple announced that Apple is ending support for Intel-powered Macs with macOS Tahoe](https://www.wired.com/story/macos-tahoe-last-update-for-intel-macs/). 2) Starting with Marvelous Designer 2024, the minimum macOS has been changed to Monterey 12. See which macs are compatible with macOS Monterey 12 here. [macOS Monterey is compatible with these computers.](https://support.apple.com/en-us/103260) 3) To use the basic functions of Marvelous Designer, 16GB of memory is required; for smoother operation, 32GB of memory is needed; and for very heavy and complex clothing and animations, 64GB or more of memory is required. * * * # **Linux** Category | **Minimum** | **Recommended** ---|---|--- OS | Rocky Linux 9.5 and its Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) equivalent | Rocky Linux 9.5 and its Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) equivalent Processor | AMD® Ryzen™ 3000 series Intel® 8th-Gen series | AMD® Ryzen™ 9000 series or higher Intel® i9 14th-Gen or higher Memory | 16GB | 64GB Graphics card | AMD, Intel, Nvidia GPUs supporting OpenGL 1.6 or higher | NVIDIA® GeForce RTX 4000 series or NVIDIA® RTX A, RTX Ada, RTX Pro Blackwell series Storage | SSD 10GB or more | SSD 20GB or more Screen | 1920x1080(FHD) | 2560x1440(QHD), 3840x2160(UHD, 4K) Input device | 3-button mouse | 3-button mouse Network | Internet connection required | Internet connection required 1) For Linux, the software is available only for Enterprise customers upon request. If you are interested in the Linux version, please visit our [Pricing page](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/pricing?type=enterprise) for more details. 2) Please see the [Setup Guide for Marvelous Designer on Linux](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/50922660869401-Setup-Guide-for-Marvelous-Designer-on-Linux) for setup instructions. 3) To use the basic functions of Marvelous Designer, 16GB of memory is required; for smoother operation, 32GB of memory is needed; and for very heavy and complex clothing and animations, 64GB or more of memory is required. * * * # **Please Note** * Marvelous Designer software does not support garment pattern digitizers. * Marvelous Designer software have tested and supports Wacom® tablet products, and compatibility issues may occur with third-party tablets. * Marvelous Designer software does not support BootCamp in macOS, also does not support similar desktop virtualization apps. * Marvelous Designer software does not support 32-bit OS (e.g. Windows 7 32-bit), Apple iOS, iPad OS, tvOS, Android OS, ChromeOS, and Windows Mobile. * Marvelous Designer software can be downloaded as .exe or .dmg file format via [Marvelous Designer official website](https://marvelousdesigner.com/product/download). It is not distributed in .msi or .pkg file format. * Marvelous Designer software can be installed and run in virtual server environments such as Virtual Machine and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure and in cloud services. However, in this case, Marvelous Designer team does not provide technical support.
content_description: This web page provides essential specifications and precautions for successfully installing and operating Marvelous Designer software on Windows, Mac, and Linux systems.

title: Lacing
content: **Ver 2026.0** **** Automate the lacing process by guiding the lacing pattern and direction through designated holes. This tool eliminates manual intervention by automatically routing the cord and generating an editable pattern for further customization. **** ### **Workflow** 1. Select the **Lacing Tool** from the 2D Toolbar. 2. Click the **starting hole** where the lacing begins or where the cord is first inserted. 3. Click the **next hole** in your desired sequence. 4. Continue clicking holes until you reach the **last** or **exit hole.** **** 5. To complete the sequence, **double-click** the final hole or press **Enter**. 6. An **editable lace pattern** will automatically generate in the 2D window for further modifications. **※ Note** * When you click the hole, press Backspace key to undo the final step. Click Esc key or Ctrl+Z key to undo the whole creation step. **** ### **Options** After finalizing the path, you can reverse its direction or adjust its curvature. #### **Reverse Direction** 1. Immediately after finalizing the path, a **reverse icon** ![Reverse.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/55655198298905)will appear attached to your cursor. 2. Click a specific hole to **reverse the lacing direction** at that point. E.g., changing if the cord enters from the top or bottom of the eyelet. 3. Check the 3D window to see the routing changes update in real-time. #### **Adjust Curvature** Adjust the cord's arc using the slider. Increasing curvature helps stabilize simulation by preventing the cord from colliding with or clipping into nearby patterns. **※ Note** * The generated lace is a standard pattern piece; you can independently edit its thickness, material, or physical properties in the Property Editor like any other garment part. * If the cord enters an eyelet from the wrong side in 3D, use the **reverse icon** to flip the orientation without redrawing the entire path.
content_description: "Effortlessly automate and customize your lacing patterns with our intuitive tool that guides you through the lacing process while allowing real-time adjustments."

title: 3D File (Alembic) Import/Export
content: ### Objective Import/Export the object, cache, normal, and animation data contained within an Alembic file (ver2.4.0). ### Location #### Import Alembic Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Alembic #### Export Alembic Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Alembic (ver6.1) Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Alembic (HDF5) / Alembic (OGAWA) ### Operation #### Import Alembic 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Alembic → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click OK. → The Import Alembic window appears. 3. Select the settings as needed and click OK. → The Alembic file is imported based on the setting. Load Type | You can choose Open or Add. ---|--- Scale | Enter a number directly or select the desired values. Axis Conversion | Change the direction of each axis of the object. (ver. 2024.0) Option | Move Garment to Start Position | Navigates to the position of the start frame of the motion that imported the garment. Move Avatar & Garment to Start Position | Navigates to the position of the start frame of the motion that imported the outfit and avatar. Export Alembic 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Alembic (HDF5) / Alembic (OGAWA) → The Open File window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and the file name. Then, click OK. → The Export Alembic window appears. 3. Select the settings as needed and click OK. → The file is exported as an Alembic file based on the setting. #### File | File Type (ver6.1) | Select a file type. ---|---|--- #### Object #### #### #### | Unweld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0. (ver2.3.0). | Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. | Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Merge Vertex by Proximity: Merge vertices across patterns by proximity Weld Turned Sewing Lines (ver 2026.0): Even when the Sewing Line Type is set to Turned, you can still merge vertices for export. Unified UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. Include Avatar Shape: Save the Avatar as part of the file. FPS | Sets the frame rate of the cache data. (below ver. 12.2) Basic | Scale the exported file by selecting the desired units or entering the percentage number. Animation | You can specify Entire Region or Play Region Only to export. Selecting the Current Frame menu allows you to export only the current frame. (ver. 2024.0) Color | You can export Strain or Stress as vertex color.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for importing and exporting Alembic files, including object, cache, normal, and animation data, with customizable settings for optimal file management.

title: 3D File (FBX) Import/Export
content: ### Objective Import a file's Geometry, Material, Joint, and Camera Animation information in the FBX file format (ver2.2.0). ### Location #### Import FBX Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ FBX #### Export FBX Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ FBX ### Operation #### Import FBX 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ FBX → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click OK. → The Import FBX window appears. 3. Select the settings and click OK. → The FBX file is imported based on the setting. Load Type | Open | All existing objects will be removed, leaving the imported FBX file only. ---|---|--- Add | Add a FBX file, keeping the existing objects. Auto Create Fitting Suit | For humanoid avatars only, a Fitting Suit is automatically created in the import process. Object Type | Avatar | Import a FBX file as an Avatar type. \- Objects imported as an Avatar type can be muti-selected. Trim | Import a FBX file as a Trim type. \- The object will pass through the clothing while Simulation is on, as the Trim type cannot collide with clothing. \- Set the collide option for a Trim type on the Property Editor by toggling on the Collision check-box. \- Select an trim object and toggle on the Glue icon on the gizmo to attach the object to clothing. \- Toggle on the Scale icon on the gizmo to scale the size of an object. Scene & Props | Import FBX file in Scene & Props format. \- You can use the Collision menu in the property window. Object | Camera | Toggles whether the Camera data or Camera Animation data is imported Joint Animation | Toggles whether the Joint Animation date is imported. Cache Animation (mc) | Toggles whether the Cache Animation data is imported. Automatically Add Arrangement Points | For humanoid avatars only, arrangement points are automatically generated in the import process. Scale | Input the Specific Value or Choose Measure. Axis Conversion | Modifying Object's Axis direction.(ver. 12.2) Translation | Align Bottom to Ground | When an object is placed below the ground, toggle on Align Bottom to Ground check-box to place the object imported above ground. Option | Move Garment to Start Position | Move the garment to the starting frame of the imported motion. #### Export FBX 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ FBX → The Save File window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and file name, and then click OK. → The Export OBJ window appears. 3. Select the settings as needed and click OK. → The file is exported as a FBX file based on the setting. Object | Select an Avatar (ver 6.1) Select the avatar to be exported. ※ Note: The selected avatar is saved with its rigging data. You can exclude it as desired. Select All Avatars (ver. 12.2) \- All existing avatars will be exported. ---|--- **Single Object** Exports the selected object as a single object. | **Multiple Objects** Exports the selected object as multiple objects. **Un-Weld** Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0 (ver2.3.0). | **Weld** Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). **Thin** Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. ※ Note: * When an object is exported as a single object, its texture is exported as a whole even when its sides (front, back, and side) have different textures (ver5.0.0.) | **Thick** Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. ※ Note: * The thickness can be exported when Pattern Mesh is Quadrangular (ver2.3.0.) * Each side's texture is exported individually when an object's front, back, side have different textures (ver5.0.0.) Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. ※Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. | Image File | Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: ‘File Name_0’, ‘File Name_1’. ---|--- Texture Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 512 ~ 8192 Pixel Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. ※ Weld Turned Sewing Lines (ver 2026.0) Even when the Sewing Line Type is set to Turned, you can still merge vertices for export. Option | Joint Animation: | Saves the animation data that was originally imported with the FBX file. **※ Changes in ver 2026.0** \- Renamed to **Avatar Joint Animation.** \- When **Bake Animation** is activated, keys are generated for every frame and exported. Cache Animation (MC) | Saves the cache data along with the recorded Garment Animation. **※ Changes in ver 2026.0** \- Renamed to **Garment Animation (MCX).** \- **Avatar Cache Animation (MCX)** can now be exported separately. Scale | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from “Unit in file to import” is selected. Axis Conversion | Changes the directions of each axis of the object. Animation | Entire Region | Exports the entire range where animation keys are set. Play Region Only | Exports only the animation within the specified playback range. File | File Type: Select between Binary or Ascii file type. * Binary: The file is saved in binary and cannot be opened by users. * Ascii: The file is saved as text and can be opened by users. Relative Texture Image File Path: Saves the texture image name without a texture image file path. Texture images are saved in the same folder as the FBX file, for automatic import. Absolute Texture Image File Path: Saves the file path that contained the texture images as the texture file path. If the texture image file path is changed, texture images cannot be imported. Save With Texture Files (.zip): Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. ※ Note: 1. FBX SDK 2020 version is available. (ver 10) * Only Joint that was imported as FBX to Marvelous Designer can be exported as FBX. 2. Import/Export FBX with multiple avatars (ver 12.2) * Multiple avatars can be imported or exported simultaneously using the FBX file format. 3. Export FBX with Material Names (Ver 2025.0) * Material Names are now synchronized exported with the FBX.
content_description: This webpage provides comprehensive instructions for importing and exporting FBX files, including geometry, materials, joint animations, and camera data, within the specified software environment.

title: 3D File (OBJ) Import/Export
content: ### OBJ Import/Export ### Objective An OBJ file is used when saving Scene and Props that organize Avatar and surrounding environment. If the OBJ type is an Avatar, the OBJ file is able to wear Garments but if it is a Trim, the Garment passes through it as it does not recognize it as an object. For detailed instruction on how to use OBJ files as Trims, refer to Load As Trim. Furthermore, OBJ files with the same Mesh structure (net-shaped structure expresses 3D objects) is able to be "Morphed" to change Avatar's appearance. “Morphing” refers to slowly changing the appearance of one object into another, and this function can be used to change Avatar's poses or body type. This function is useful when changing Poses of an Avatar in Garments. For detailed instruction, refer to Load as Morph Target. Garments made with Marvelous Designer are able to be formatted/imported in *.obj file and they are compatible with other 3D software. When exporting Garments in an *.obj file, a *.mtl file is also created, and this *.mtl file saves material information of the Garment. ### Location #### OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Additional OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ #### OBJ Export Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ OBJ #### Selected OBJ Export Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ OBJ (Selected) ### Operation #### OBJ Import 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Select a file and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: #### OBJ Import Detail Settings Object Type | Load as Avatar | Imports an object as an avatar and replaces it with the original avatar. Add Arrangement Points &BVs: Turn on this option to generate Bounding Volumes and Arrangement Points fit to the imported OBJ (ver4.2.0). ※Note: This option works properly only when imported OBJ is either in T or A pose and below error message appears when this function cannot be applied properly. "Arrangement Points were not fitted to the avatar. The avatar must be in a T-pose or A-pose." ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438250166297) ---|---|--- Load as Trim | Due to nonfunctional collision detection, objects pass through garments (ver3.0.0). Load as Garment | Import an object as a 3D Garment. Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map: Toggle on this option to generate Patterns based on UV Map information (ver4.2.0). Load as Morph Target | Morphs the original object into the object designated as the Morph Target. Enter the Transition Frame Count. The higher the frame count, the slower the morphing process. Scale | Manually enters values or selects the desired unit. Axis Conversion | Changes the directions of each axis of an object. When the OBJ is placed below the ground, please toggle on Align Bottom to Ground option to pull up the OBJ file above the ground (ver4.2.0). ※ Note: Load as Garment - Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map #### OBJ Additional Import 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ → The Add File window appears. 2. Set details and click OK. #### OBJ Export 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ OBJ (Selected) → Save File window appears. 2. Select desired location to store, and click Save. → Export OBJ window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: #### OBJ Export Detail Settings Object | Select All Patterns: Select/Deselect all Patterns. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). ※ Note: If OBJ(Selected) is utilized, selected Patterns are being checked in the 3D and 2D window. Select All Avatars: Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Select All Graphics/Top-stitches: Select/Deselect all Graphics/Top-stitches. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). ---|--- #### Single Object Exports selected object as a single object. | #### Multiple Objects Exports selected object as multiple objects. #### Unweld Exports Vertex(points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects. | #### Weld Combines Vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts together as one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld sewing-lines of selected patterns. #### Thin Ensures thickness is not exported to Geometry even if the value is increased beforehand. | #### Thick Exports thickness value to Geometry. ※ Note: Thickness is available to be exported when pattern's mesh is Quad (ver2.3.0). Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. ※Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. | Image File | Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: ‘File Name_0’, ‘File Name_1’. ---|--- Texture Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 100 ~ 10000 Pixel Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. ※ Weld Turned Sewing Lines (ver 2026.0) Even when the Sewing Line Type is set to Turned, you can still merge vertices for export. Include Internal Shape: Includes internal line and/or shape information in export (ver2.3.0). Scale | Adjusts scale of file being exported when a value is entered or desired unit from 'Unit in file to import' is selected. Axis Conversion | Changes directions of object's each axis. File | Save with Texture File (*.zip): Exports .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: When color is applied to the texture, the color is blended into the texture when exporting (ver4.2.0). Exclude Ambient Map & Color (Modo): Ambient Map and color are excluded when exporting (ver4.2.0). Save with Alpha Map: Alpha Map is included when exporting (ver4.2.0). Save with Meta Data (*.xml) : Exports garment's pattern(Mesh), physical property and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0). Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: Combine and save garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0). Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo): Exclude Ambient color value when saving materials. ※ Note: #### OBJ Export Updates Internal Line(s)/Shape(s) export (including FBX). Thickness export for Quad Mesh. Front, side and back meshes separate export. * * * ### ### Load as Garment ### Objective Import and simulate OBJ files from other 3D software programs (Maya, 3DS MAX and etc). ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ to Garment ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ to Garment → Open File window appears. 2. Select a file and click OK. → OBJ to Garment window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ### Load as Morph Target ### Objective Morph uses two different OBJ files to slowly change object's appearance. Marvelous Designer's default avatars can be modified at Change Avatar Size menu or posed with Show X-Ray Joints function, other 3D software may not have basic Joints set for designed objects, parts may be lost when creating a compatible COLLADA file. As such, this menu can be used to change the object's body type. At least two *.obj files with the same Mesh structure are needed to morph the object. Use this menu to import objects from different 3D software as Avatars, and dress them or change their Poses. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438235048217) ### Location #### Import OBJ Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Open Morph Target OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Morph Target ### Operation 1. Choose two *.obj files to morph. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 3. Select the first file to import and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 4. Set details and click OK. 5. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 6. Select the second file to import and click OK. → Open Morph Target window appears. 7. Follow the indicated guideline: OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Morph Target 8. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: File name with #(special character) is not going to be loaded. ### Load as Trim ### Objective Use *.obj files designed in other 3D software to organize Trims as well as the Avatars in Garments. When loading a file as an Avatar, the Garment registers the object as an Avatar and allows to drape on top of it, however when the same file is loaded as Trims, the Garment does not register it as an object therefore it passes through it. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438250539289) ### Location #### OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Import as Scene/Prop OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Trim ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Choose file to import and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 3. Select Load as Trim in Object Type. 4. Set details and click OK. ### Load as Avatar ### Objective Use *.obj files designed in other 3D software to use as Avatars in Marvelous Designer. When loading a file as an Avatar, the Garment registers the object as an Avatar and allows to drape on top of it. ### Location #### OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Import as Scene/Prop OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Avatar ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Choose file to import and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 3. title: ZIPPER: Registering Custom OBJ to Component
content: ### Objective Allows the user to create custom components for zippers that function dynamically in the 3D Window exactly as default provided zipper components. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Zipper ▶ Register OBJ 3D Toolbar ▶ Zipper Tool ▶ Property Editor ▶ Type ▶ '+' ### Operation #### Workflow 1. Create mesh for Zipper Components(Puller, Slider, Teeth, and Stopper) export as an OBJ. → If creating a single OBJ file for both Slider & Puller, the node for the Slider must be named "Slider," and the node for the Puller must be named "Puller" before export. 2. Navigate to either of the locations listed above under "Location" and click on 'Register OBJ' or the '+' icon in the Property Editor. 3. Select the relevant Type (Slider, Puller, Slider & Puller, Teeth, Stopper). 4. In the File section of the Register OBJ dialog, click on the four-square button to navigate to the location of the custom OBJ file and Double-Click to select it. 5. Adjust the position of the Puller or Slider in the preview window. 6. Click 'OK'. 7. Load a garment with a Zipper. 8. Click on the Zipper in the 3D Window. 9. In the Property Editor for the Zipper, observe that the Slider, Puller, Teeth or Stopper the user has registered is now available to be assigned to the zipper. → You can find the custom Zipper component in the dropdown menu to the right of Slider or Puller under the 'Type' section. #### Options The options for the Register OBJ dialog are as follows. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Basic** | **Type** | Select the type (Slider, Puller, Slider & Puller, Teeth, and Stopper) to register the OBJ. **Name** | Enter a file name. **Scale** | Adjust the size of the OBJ. **Axis Conversion** | Change each axis of the OBJ. **File** | **OBJ** | Slider / Puller | Load the OBJ file you want to register. Stopper (Top, Bottom-Open) | Load each Top and Botton-Open OBJ file. The first OBJ loaded is placed in the direction of the zipper created first. Slider & Puller | Load a combined zipper OBJ file. Select and assign the mesh item of Slider and Puller in the Select Mesh menu. Teeth (ver 2026.0) | Load the OBJ file to register as the zipper teeth. The spacing between the teeth is set to 0 mm by default. Adjust the spacing while previewing the result in the preview window. **Preview** | Check the imported OBJ file in advance. Space | When registering teeth, set the spacing for individual teeth objects. **Puller Position** | For Slider or Slider & Puller type. Adjust the sliders on the X, Y, and Z axes to set where the puller is attached.
content_description: This web page enables users to dynamically create and register custom 3D zipper components for enhanced garment design within the platform.

title: UV EDITOR MODE: Edit UV location
content: UV Display UV Selection Arraying individual UV Arraying all UV UV Packing * * * ### UV Display (ver 2026.0) To control the UV display targets, click the UV Display icon in the UV Editor and select a display method. Refer to the following to select the UV display target: **Options** | **Description** ---|--- **UV Display Target** | **Show All Objects** | Displays the UVs of all garments and avatars in the scene. **Show Selected Objects** | Displays only the UVs of the selected garments and avatars. **※ Note:** The UV Display Element cannot be controlled when this option is activated. **UV Display Element** | **Show Garment** | Displays the UVs of garments. **Show Avatar** | Displays the UVs of avatars. * * * ### UV Selection UVs can be selected in several ways as described below. **Select All with Same Property** and **Select All Sewn Patterns** can be executed from the right-click pop-up menu of the selected UV. **Single Selection** | Click to select the desired UV. Hold Shift and click to add UVs to the previous selection. Multiple UVs can be selected by dragging. ---|--- **Select All with Same Property** | **Particle Distance** | Selects all Patterns that have the same particle distance. **Layer** | Selects all Patterns that have the same layer value. **Fabric** | Selects all Patterns with the same applied fabric. **Select All Sewn Patterns** | Selects all Patterns that have a direct or indirect sewing relationship with the selected Pattern. * * * ### Arraying individual UV #### Objective Arraying selected individual UV. #### Location Window ▶ UV editor mode ▶ UV right-click popup menu Viewport Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ UV Editor ▶ UV right-click popup menu (ver. 2025.0) #### Operation Align | Left, Center, Right, Top, Middle, Bottom | Selected UVs will be aligned by a selected standard. Align menu will be displayed when selecting more than two UVs. ---|---|--- Flip Horizontally | Selected UV will be flipped left and right. Flip Vertically | Selected UV will be flipped up and down. Fit UV to 0-1 | Selected UV will be aligned to 0-1 coordinates. (ver. 10) * Length (Absolute): the actual distance * UV Coordinate (Relative): The ratio of 0-1 length to 1. The maximum distance is 0.4. * * * ### Arraying all UV #### Objective Arraying all UV visible in UV editor mode. #### Location UV editor mode Right-click on background #### Operation Fit All UV to unified (0-1) | All UV will be aligned to 0-1 coordinates. Tile padding option Set the distance between the pattern and the outline in the dialog. * Length (Absolute): the actual distance * UV Coordinate (Relative): The ratio of 0-1 length to 1. The maximum distance is 0.4. ---|--- Set UV from pattern alignment | Location of all UV will be re-arranged as 2D pattern window. Zoom Extents All | Set the view in the UV window to reveal all patterns. (ver. 10) Show Wire | Disable texture and show mesh view. (ver. 9.5 below) * * * ### UV Packing #### Objective The selected UV shells can be automatically packed into the targeted UV tile. #### Location UV Editor ▶ Toolbar ▶ UV Packing #### Operation 1. Select desired UV shells to be packed. \- Ctrl+A can be used to select all existing UV shells. 2. Follow the dedicated path found in Location above to open Dialog box: Padding | Set the interval between UV shells. Unit: Permille (‰) of UV tile size. Min: 0.001 ~ Max: 0.999 ---|--- Packing Ratio (Archived since version 2024.1) | The percentage of area occupied by UV shells, compared to the size of the selected UV tile. Min: 80 ~ Max: 99 * 95% is the recommended input value. Higher values take more time to pack the UV shells. Fidelity (ver.2024.1) | The larger the value, the more sensitively the shape of the UV shell is calculated. Min: 1 ~ Max: 5 ![Fidelity.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438275643161) Fix Scale Ratio | Fix the current ratio of UV shells. Rotation | Allow UV shells to be rotated if needed. Advanced Placement (Ver. 2024.1) | Numerous sequences are tested to find a better placement to create least empty space. UV Area | Set the target UV tile to pack the selected UV shells. Reset | Reset all inputs in dialog box to default. Apply | All inputs will be applied to the UV shells and tiles. Close | Close the dialog box ※ Note: * When Advanced Placement is turned off, UV shells are placed sequentially from largest to smallest. * Advanced Placement option will decrease speed. Unless in extreme situations, it is recommended to turn Advanced Placement on.

title: Blend Shape Avatar
content: **ver 2026.0** **** Blend Shape is a technology that creates natural forms by blending various pre-made body types or facial expressions at desired ratios. With just a single base model, Blend Shape allows for real-time and flexible transformations, ranging from various target body sizes to subtle facial expressions. This feature enables users to import avatars containing Blend Shape data into Marvelous Designer, allowing for instantaneous body changes and precise dynamic fitting. **📝 Note:** To use this feature, you should import files that contain Blend Shape data. ### **Workflow** 1. Load a file containing Blend Shape data as an Avatar type. 2. Go to Main Menu → Avatar → **Avatar Editor** to open the Avatar Editor 3. Click on the **Blend Shape** tab in the Avatar Editor 4. Check the list of **Deformable Parameters** included in the loaded avatar. 5. Adjust the weight of the desired part between 0 and 100 to modify the shape. #### ### **Options** 1. Select Avatar * This option is displayed when multiple Blend Shape avatars are loaded; it will not appear if only a single avatar is present. * Selecting an avatar will display the corresponding Deformable Parameters for that specific avatar. 2. Deformable Parameters * The list of deformable parameters included by the creator is grouped and displayed by mesh unit. * Each parameter can be set as a **Favorite**. By enabling **Show Favorites Only** in the top right, you can manage the list efficiently by displaying only your favorited items. * Clicking the **Reset** button will revert all unsaved changes to their initial values.
content_description: Discover how to leverage Blend Shape technology in Marvelous Designer for real-time, flexible transformations of avatars, enabling effortless adjustments of body types and facial expressions.

title: Create Smooth Curve
content: ### ### ### ### ### Objective Modify Pattern outlines or Internal Lines into smooth curves. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar ▶ Smooth Curve ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar ▶ Smooth Curve 2. Click on a segment or point to establish the first point. → The point appears in grey. ※ Note: (Ver 2026.0) If you click where segments/lines overlap, a menu will pop up. Simply choose whether you want to start on the Pattern Outline or Internal Line. 3. Drag the mouse. → A grey arrow extending from the point follows the cursor. 4. Click on another segment or point to establish the endpoint. → A reference line is created between the two points. 5. With the reference line created, click on the side that will be converted into a smooth curve. → The entire side is highlighted in yellow. 6. Click & drag the reference line to create the desired smooth curve. → The entire outline of the selected side is replaced by the reference line. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438534208793) ### Updated in 2025.0 Curvature of a specific line can be precisely adjusted without affecting other lines. 1. Click a start point and endpoint on the segment or point to set the editing range. 2. Select which side to be edited. 3. Click and drag a segment or point to adjust curvature within the set range. * **Edit** * By default, nearby points adjust proportionally when moving. * You can move only the selected point by holding the [ D ] key while dragging. * Right-click while dragging the segment or point to enter a specific moving distance. * **Add** * Click a segment while holding the [ Ctrl ] key to add a curve point. _* Adding to a Bezier curve points convert it to free curve points, which may adjust the curvature._ * **Delete** * Right-click a point and click the Delete menu to delete selected points. 4. Press Enter to complete. * When selecting a pattern outline or internal line, update based on the edited pattern outline or internal line. * When selecting a reference line, update based on the edited reference line. Segment points will be added at the start and end. * ※ Note: #### Cancel Actions * Cancel All Actions: While using the Smooth Curve tool, press Esc or Ctrl + Z on the keyboard and all actions are undone. * Cancel Last Action: While using the Smooth Curve tool, press Delete or Backspace on the keyboard and the last action is undone.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions on how to modify pattern outlines and internal lines into smooth curves using the Smooth Curve tool in the 2D Pattern editing menu.

title: Animation Marker
content: #### **New in 2026.0** **** Animation Markers indicate significant points on the timeline or in space, allowing users to quickly identify the locations of scene transitions, events, and keyframes. Comments can be added to Markers to leave notes regarding editing intentions or task instructions. Additionally, they can be utilized as event triggers in the API via their names. ## **Add** 1. Open the **Animation Editor**. 2. Right-click the **Timeline Ruler** to display the context menu. 3. Click **Add** under the Marker group. 4. When the Marker dialog appears, set the name and frame of the Marker, then click OK. 5. Verify that a new Marker has been created at the specified frame. #### ## **Edit** 1. Hover the mouse over a created Marker to view its name and frame through the displayed tooltip. 2. To move a Marker, select and drag it to the left or right. 3. To edit a Marker's name, double-click the Marker or right-click it and select Edit from the context menu. 4. Modify the information in the displayed dialog, then click OK. 5. Verify that the changes have been applied to the Marker. #### ## **Copy and Paste** 1. Select one or more Markers. 2. Copy the Markers by pressing Ctrl+C or clicking Copy from the right-click context menu. 3. Specify the current frame using the playhead, then paste the Markers by pressing Ctrl+V or clicking Paste from the context menu. 4. The Markers will be pasted at the current frame indicated by the playhead. #### ## **Delete** 1. Select one or more Markers you wish to delete. 2. Press the Delete key or click Delete from the right-click context menu to remove the Markers.
content_description: Discover the powerful new Animation Markers feature in version 2026.0, designed to streamline your editing process by allowing you to easily add, edit, copy, and delete markers for scene transitions and keyframes while enhancing collaboration through comments and event triggers

title: ZIPPER: Create Zippers
content: ### Objective Create and use Zippers quickly and easily. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Zipper ▶ Zipper 3D Toolbar ▶ Zipper ### Operation 1. Navigate to the location listed below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Zipper 2. Click on the 3D garment or 2D Patterns (ver MD10) where the Zipper should be attached, then move the cursor. → Based on the direction the cursor is moved, the segment where the Zipper appears is highlighted in light blue. 3. Double click on the desired endpoint for the Zipper. → One side of the Zipper is created. 4. Click on the Pattern outline where the other side of the Zipper is attached, then move the cursor. → Based on the direction the cursor is moved, a blue point appears indicating the same length as the first half of the Zipper which was created in step 3. 5. Double click on the blue point. → The Zipper is now complete, along with a Puller, Slider, and Stopper (ver MD10). 6. Activate the Simulation. → The Zipper simulates in a closed/fully zipped state. → To unzip the Zipper, click on the Zipper in the 3D Window WITHOUT the Gizmo active, and drag to move the Zipper (referenced in dark grey) along the length of the Zipper Tape. ※ Note: #### Cancel Actions during Zipper Creation * Cancel All Actions While using the Zipper tool, press 'Esc' or 'Ctlr +Z' on the keyboard, and all actions will be undone. * Cancel Last Action While using the Zipper tool, press the 'Delete' or 'Backspace' Key on the keyboard and the last action will be undone.
content_description: This web page provides a quick and easy guide to creating and manipulating zippers within your 3D garment or 2D patterns using the Zipper tool.

title: Express Cartoon
content: **Ver 2026.0** **** This feature allows for a unique cartoon-style look using fabric, 3D objects and avatar materials. ### **Workflow** 1. Select a fabric style or an avatar. 2. In the Property Editor, set Material ▶ Type ▶**Toon** 3. Adjust the displayed property values to achieve your desired style. #### ### **Options** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Base Color** | **Color** | Corresponds to MToon’s Lit Color parameter, representing the original color visible when receiving 100% light. **Base Color Map** | The texture map used for the Base Color **Opacity** | **Opacity** | Transparency settings for the Base Color. The overall transparency value. **Opacity Map** | Apply Common UI for assigning Texture Maps / Adding Maps. **Shade** | **Color** | The RGB color of the shadow. **Shade Color Map** | A texture applied specifically to shadow areas. Often uses the same texture as the Base Color or is left empty. **Hardness** | The degree of sharpness of the shadow edges. **Shift** | Adjusts the threshold where shadows begin to form. Higher values result in larger shadow areas. **Emission** | **Color** | Configures the parts that glow self-luminously, unaffected by external lighting. The color that glows brightly even in dark environments. **Emission Map** | The texture map used for parts that glow in the dark. **MatCap** | **Color** | MatCap is a fake refelction effect. The color to be blended with the MatCap image. **Matcap Map** | A texture that stores pre-captured ambient lighting information, layering a glossy effect on the surface based on the camera's viewing angle. **Rim Light** | **Color** | Rim Light(Halo) effect formed on the inner edges of the character. **Fresnel Power** | Adjusts the thickness and sharpness of the rim light. Controls the falloff of the light-affected area. **Lift** | Adjusts the position offset of the rim light. **Outline** | **Mode** | Creates a border line to achieve a cartoon-like aesthetic. Mode is the method of generating the outline. **Outline Map** | A texture used for masking to prevent outlines from appearing on specific areas. **Color** | The color of the line. **Width (mm)** | The thickness of the line.
content_description: Discover how to create a unique cartoon-style look for your projects using fabric, 3D objects, and customizable avatar materials with our comprehensive guide.

title: Steam
content: ## Objective Shrink or stretch Fabric partially like as using a steam iron. ## Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Steam ▶ Steam 2D Toolbar ▶ Steam ## Operation #### Steam Setting 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Steam ▶ Steam 2D Toolbar ▶ Steam → All Patterns are now being displayed in mesh. → The Steam Brush appears at the top-left corner of the 2D window. 2. Set the value as desired. Mode (v2026.0) | Add | Operates as a brush that adds Steam. ---|---|--- Remove | Sets Operates as a brush that removes Steam. Option | Shrinkage | Sets the shrinkage level. Size | Sets the size of the brush. Hardness | Sets the hardness of the steam. 3. Click and drag on desired area to steam. → According to the shrinkage, the selected area is now being displayed in light-blue or orange. 4. Activate the Simulate. #### Remove Steam 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Steam ▶ Steam 2D Toolbar ▶ Steam 2. Right-click on a pattern to remove steam, and select either Remove Steam on Selected Pattern or Remove All Steam. → The steam is now being deleted accordingly. ※ Note: It can also be removed from the same right-click pop-up menu with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools.

title: 3D Pencil (Avatar)
content: **Ver 2026.0** **** Sketch directly on the avatar and turn your lines into patterns instantly. #### **Sketch** 1. Load an avatar in the 3D window to being sketching. 2. In the 3D toolbar, press and hold the **3D Pen (Avatar)** and switch to the **3D Pencil (Avatar)**. → The Sketch dialog appears, and the viewpoint switches to the front view. **※ Note:** To ensure proper conversion to 3D Pen after sketching, the 3D view is fixed to either the front or back view. Only zooming is available. 3. Click and drag on the avatar to sketch your design. 4. Change the type to **Eraser** , then click and drag over the area you want to remove. → The lines within the dragged area are removed. #### **Options** 1. Set the following options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Type** | **Pencil** | **Symmetry** | Applies symmetrical sketching based on the avatar’s center axis. **Conversion** **Guide** | Before converting to 3D Pen, you can see how your sketch will be converted. The segment points shown on the guide line are important, as areas without points will turn into curves. If you need a corner or a defined angle, make sure a point is present at that position. If a corner is missing a point, the edge may become rounded unintentionally. We recommend reviewing the guide and adjusting your lines to achieve the best results before converting. **Eraser** | **Size** | Adjust the eraser size to control how much is removed at once. **Viewpoint** | Switch the 3D viewpoint to either the front or back. #### **Convert to 3D Pen** 1. Click the **Convert to 3D Pen** in the Sketch dialog. → The lines drawn on the avatar are converted to 3D Pen, and the tool automatically switches to the **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar).** 2. Check the converted 3D Pen and edit[ ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115008890367-Edit-3D-Pen-Avatar)it directly as needed. **※ Note:**__ For 3D Pens created by sketching on both the front and back simultaneously, flattening both sides automatically sews the front and back together.
content_description: Discover how to effortlessly sketch on avatars and transform your designs into stunning 3D patterns with our intuitive 3D Pen and Pencil tools.

title: Sewing Line Type
content: ### Objective Apply the Turned Sewing Line type setting to achieve a folded, two ply look. ![Sewing](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438733625881) ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ (Select Sewing Line) Property Editor ▶ Sewing Line Type 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ (Select Sewing Line) Property Editor ▶ Sewing Line Type ### Operation 1. title: Pattern Drafter (Beta)
content: **New in 2025.1** Open Measurement Options Edit Pattern AI Pattern Drafter (Beta) **** Easily Create your First Pattern within Marvelous Designer, using either measurement points or your flat sketches. **** ### **Open** 1. Click the 2D ▶ **Pattern Drafter (Beta)** in the top menu. 2. Choose the type of Shirt Style. 3. From there you will then see your Simple Measurements Populate below. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/49696317429785) **** ### **Measurements Options** 1. You have 3 different options for how you want to view and adjust your measurements for you patterns. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **General** | This will give you a complete list of the most commonly used Points of Measure for that style. **Simple** | This will give you the most commonly used points of measure for simple editing of patterns. **Custom** | This is automatically adjust to Custom when you select your own measurement list and customize to your preference. 1\. Click ![setting.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950075963417) **Setting** button to view the full list of measurements. 2\. Once setup is complete, click ![Total-1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950075968153) **Exit** button to apply changes. 2. Enter your pattern measurement values. _**✨Tip:** _ ▪️You can return each measurement to its original value individually by clicking ![reset.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950075972761) **Reset** button. ▪️Certain Measurements include ![Total.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950075974169)**Total** option to input the full front and back circumference. ▪️Certain measurements include dropdown options, as they are commonly taken from different areas of the pattern. **\- Total Length:** High Point Shoulder, Or Center Front/ Back **\- Across Front/ Back:** 4", 5" or 6" from High Point shoulder **\- Across Waist:** 4", 5" or 6" from Armhole **\- Across Bust/ Chest:** Armhole to Armhole or 1" from Armhole **\- Bicep Width:** Armhole to Armhole or 1" from Armhole ▪️For the Front and Back Body, you can choose between **Symmetry** and **Half Symmetry**. ▪️You can view all inactive measurements in each section by clicking ![list.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950075975321) **Show All Measurements** icon. #### #### ### **Edit Pattern (ver 2026.0)** Patterns created with Pattern Drafter can be edited while retaining their original parameters. 1. Open the Pattern Drafter. → If a parametric pattern exists, select whether to create a new pattern or edit it. 2. Select the ![Frame 215.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/56586933637529) button. → The pattern type is automatically detected. 3. Change the measurement values, then click the ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/56586900700953)**** button. Or, click ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/56586900704025) button to generate a new parametric pattern. ### **AI Pattern Drafter (Beta)** Using a Sketch Marvelous Designer will Automatically generate measurements to create a drafted pattern for you. 1. Click ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/49886528028441) **AI Pattern Drafter (Beta)** button on the top right of the Pattern Drafter. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950276717721) 2. Generate a background image to be composited by entering prompts or upload it directly. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Text Prompt** | Select the garment type and write in your sketch idea. Make sure to add in as many descriptive words as possible. if you want to emphasize something place it in brackets. ※ Supporting Type: **T-Shirts, Pants, and Skirts.** (There will be more coming.) **✨ Writing Tips:** Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. ![Comment.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950284431001)**Keyword Suggestions** | Suggested keywords will appear as you type to help you complete your prompt. ![icon_pin_off.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950276732057)**Maintain Prompt** | Even if the same prompts are used, the AI Face image is created anew each time. Thus, clicking the Maintain Prompt button may update the prompts while preserving the existing results as much as possible. The results may differ from the existing ones depending on the addition or change of the prompts. ![icon_random_dice.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950276734489) **Random** | Sample prompts are provided randomly ![Editor Edit.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950276735257) **Clear** | Clear anything that was written to restart. **Image** | Click the **Upload** button to load a face image that fits the following guidelines: A schematic image of the garment with black lines on a white background is highly recommended to ensure the highest quality of the AI Pattern. Ensure the image shows the garment only. 3. Click ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950276738969) button and an image will be generated for you to choose from. This process can be replicated until you get the desired outcome. Your image history can be found on the right side of the window.
content_description: Discover the new **Pattern Drafter (Beta)** and **AI Pattern Drafter** in Marvelous Designer 2025.1, allowing you to effortlessly create and customize garment patterns using measurement points or your sketches.
